html:
The Enlhet are an Indigenous people of the central Paraguayan Chaco, part of the Gran Chaco, a dry plain of thorn forest and grassland. They are close kin of the Enxet to the south, and outsiders long called both peoples Lengua.

They lived by hunting, fishing, gathering and small gardens, moving with the seasons. From 1927 Mennonite settlers from Canada, and later from Russia, founded colonies such as Menno and Fernheim on Enlhet land, with the backing of the Paraguayan state. The Chaco War with Bolivia from 1932 to 1935 brought armies and disease. Many Enlhet ended up working on Mennonite farms, and most now live in settlements near the colonies, keeping their language alive. Their northern neighbours are the Ayoreo.
